fields.meta_title: Summer Camp Registration Form Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Make a summer camp registration form that prices each week and takes a deposit at signup. Each camper is saved to a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a Summer Camp Registration Form for the Whole Season
fields.hero_description: Build a summer camp registration form that totals each family's weeks at checkout and keeps every camper on file.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Does Before Day One
fields.features_subheading: Six parts of registration that a camp office would otherwise track in a spreadsheet.
fields.feature_1:
Sessions parents tick, each with a limit

List every week or session with its dates and the ages it serves. Parents tick the ones they want, and a session stops taking campers once it reaches the limit you set for it.
fields.feature_2:
Deposits and balances through Stripe

Connect Stripe and take a deposit or the full fee when the parent submits. Each camper's row shows what was paid and what is still owed, plus the date the balance falls due.
fields.feature_3:
Allergy and medication answers

Ask about allergies and daily medications in a section of their own. Counselors open a list for their group that shows what each parent wrote, next to the camper's name.
fields.feature_4:
Waivers signed inside the form

Give the activity waiver and photo permission their own screens, each ending in a signature box. The parent's signature is kept on the camper's record with the time it was signed.
fields.feature_5:
Rosters for each cabin or group

Sort registered campers into groups by age or by cabin. Each counselor opens a roster for one group that lists the adults allowed at pickup and a phone number for each.
fields.feature_6:
The app's code, yours to keep

Export the full registration app to GitHub on paid plans when a developer wants to add a parent portal or a staff schedule. The camp's own domain is included and uses credits.

fields.usecase_heading: Registration at Four Kinds of Camp
fields.tab_content_1:
Six weeks for two children at a sibling rate

Pinecrest Day Camp charges $240 a week, and a second child from the same family gets 10% off. The Hale family enrolls Mia and Leo for 3 weeks each. Before paying, the parent sees Mia's weeks at $720 and Leo's at $648, for a total of $1,368. Both children go onto the roster for every week their parent picked.
fields.tab_content_2:
Bunk requests that both campers made rise to the top

Campers at Camp Alder Lake can name up to 2 bunkmates on the registration form. When two campers name each other, the pair is marked mutual and sorted to the top of the cabin board. One-way requests sit below them for the director to weigh. Cabin planning starts from the matched pairs.
fields.tab_content_3:
$100 to hold a seat, $350 due June 1

The Circuit Lab runs its robotics camp for $450. Parents pay a $100 deposit through Stripe when they register, and the camper's row records a $350 balance due June 1. On May 25, any family whose balance is still open gets an email reminder. Families who paid in full hear nothing.
fields.tab_content_4:
Register before May and pay $185

Cedar Hill Church takes its youth group to a lake camp each July. Parents who register by April 30 pay $185. From May 1 the price is $210, and the form charges whichever applies on the day the parent submits. The youth pastor's list shows 31 campers at the early price and 9 at the regular one.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Camp Registration Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a summer camp registration form around your sessions and test it before families sign up.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Lay out the summer week by week
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Price the sibling and early-bird rules
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 List the camper details staff need
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down each week or session your camp runs, along with the ages it serves. Give every line a price and the number of campers it takes. A half-day week and an overnight session are separate lines, each with its own limit.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Turn every discount into a sentence the form can apply: a lower rate for a second child, or a cheaper price for anyone who registers before a set date. Note whether a deposit holds the spot and when the remaining balance falls due.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide what counselors must know about each camper, such as allergies and the adults allowed at pickup. Keep the list short enough for a parent to finish in one sitting, and move optional questions to the end.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Give each waiver its own screen and end it with a signature box. If your camp runs swimming or off-site trips, name each activity on the waiver so parents can see exactly what they are agreeing to before they sign.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the session list and the pricing rules into one prompt, with the camper questions below them. Emergent builds the form and the payment step, with a database of campers and families behind them. Ask for changes the same way, such as adding a late-August week.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Decide what a full session does
fields.howto_step_6_des: Choose what parents see once a session fills. A waitlist suits a popular week. For other weeks, a note pointing to the next open session keeps families from giving up. Put the choice for each session into the prompt.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Register two made-up children as a parent would, paying with a test card. Check that the sibling rate and the deposit show correctly on each camper's row. Delete the test records before the link goes out to families.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is template pages (AidaForm, Wufoo, Jotform), a Google Docs print form, Pinterest printables and one camp's own PDF. Each gives a camp one camper on paper or in a generic builder. Directors running a season need what those pages skip: prices that change with weeks and siblings, bunk requests sorted before cabins are set, deposits with a balance due later and an early-bird cutoff. This page shows four kinds of camps running registration that way.

A church youth camp charges $185 to anyone who registers by April 30 and $210 after, and the form picks the price from the date the parent submits.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Summer Camp Registration Form for the Whole Season'; hero 'Build a summer camp registration form that totals each family's weeks at checkout and keeps every camper on file.'

intent.evidence: Top 10 is camp forms, Jotform templates and a RegFox how-to; page gives what to include (FAQ 7, 10), template answers (FAQ 3, 9) and a 7-step how-to ending in a test registration.

specificity.evidence: 'Register two made-up children as a parent would, paying with a test card.' Bunk requests, sibling rate, deposit with balance due, early-bird cutoff.

openers.evidence: Tabs open on full sentences ('Pinecrest Day Camp charges $240 a week'); features open on verbs ('List every week', 'Connect Stripe', 'Ask about allergies').

craft.evidence: No tacked-on endings; sentence lengths vary; FAQ 9 directness noted.

voice.evidence: 'One-way requests sit below them for the director to weigh.' 'Families who paid in full hear nothing.'

truth.evidence: Math checks: 3 x $240 = $720, Leo $648 at 10% off, $1,368 total; $450 - $100 = $350; 31 + 9 = 40. Claims map to approved ids; custom domain 'included and uses credits'; GitHub 'on paid plans'.

distinct.evidence: Season pricing angle (weeks, siblings, bunks, deposits, early-bird) separates it from registration-form and daycare/student siblings; registration form linked once.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions; hub link in item 2; links to emergency contact form, liability waiver form, registration form; no AlsoAsked candidates for this page; moat lines in items 3, 5, 9.

images.evidence: Hale family $720 / $648 / $1,368; Ava Brooks and Nora Kim mutual at top, June Patel one-way; Theo Marsh $100 deposit, $350 due June 1, reminder May 25; Grace Owens April 28 at $185, 31 early and 9 regular.
